0 m · The Marina

Blazing fast,
on-demand images.

The URL is the API. Write the operations into it, sign it, and crabcrop answers with the picture. A Rust-built image server in one binary: no pre-generated thumbnails, no build step.

curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -LsSf https://github.com/dayvson/crabcrop/releases/latest/download/crabcrop-installer.sh | sh
  1. Scroll to dive
  2. Make 5 choices
  3. Copy your URL

Snap’s story

A gust lifts Snap’s favorite photo print from his claw, and it sinks. He doesn’t hesitate: he grabs the anchor chain and goes after it.

−5 m · The Shallows

One URL does the whole job.

A crabcrop URL reads left to right: a signature, then the operations, then the source. Yours is in the bar at the top. It starts with our picks, and each of the five choices on the way down swaps one part of it, which lights up. On the way back up, you’ll see them go onto Snap’s print one by one.

  • Picka format · choice 1 of 5
  • Hoverthe cargo · five kinds of source
  • Tapthe cargo · five kinds of source

https://img.example.com/3843ad67…/crop:1200x630:smart/filters:sharpen(1.2):saturation(1.1)/root:photos/print.jpg

Signed URLs, from any stack

Every URL carries an HMAC-SHA256 signature over the operations and the source. Same inputs, same URL, from any of these:

  • TypeScript
  • Python
  • Rust
  • curl
Read the docs on signing

All major formats, in and out

JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, AVIF, and JPEG XL, in and out. Name no format and the browser’s Accept header decides, with ties going to AVIF, then JPEG XL, then WebP.

format(avif) · format(jxl) · format(webp)

Read the docs on formats
Choice 1 of 5Pick a format

Each school of fish is one format.

With no format named, the schools race to Snap, and the best one your browser accepts wins.

No format named: the browser’s Accept header decides.

Sources beyond photos

51 filters, one chain.

The filters chain inside one filters: segment and run in the order written. Resize, crop, fit-in, and pad each get a path segment of their own.

Chained filters

Sharpen, saturate, tone, blur, duotone, and more, chained in one filters: segment and applied in the order you write them.

Size, crop, fit, and pad

Resize to exact pixels, crop to a window that finds the subject, fit inside a box, or pad out to a shape. Each is its own path segment.

crop:1200x630:smart · fit-in:1200x630 · pad:1200x630:ffd88a

Read the docs on sizing

preset:og-card = crop:1200x630:smart/filters:format(webp):quality(80)

Presets and purge

Server-side preset names keep templates short. Purge one result, or a whole preset group, with a signature only your secret can make.

preset:og-card POST /purge-group

Read the docs on presets

It sees what matters.

Smart crops that keep faces whole, face detection, redaction, and object removal. Snap swims the reef past all four.

Here you can

  • Scrollto swim the reef · four stops
  • Picka crop · choice 3 of 5

Smart crop, face safe

Ask for any shape and the crop window moves to the subject. Faces stay whole, never cut at the edge.

crop:1200x630:smart

Read the docs on smart crop
Choice 3 of 5Pick a crop

Three shapes. The frame finds the turtle in each.

1200 × 630, the window moved to the subject.

Face detection

A YuNet model finds every face in a picture. Crop to the largest, or blur them all. All seven of these fish count.

crop:760x760:face filters:blurfaces

Read the docs on face detection

Redaction

Blur a whole class of thing, like people (the cuttlefish stands in for one here), before a picture goes out. It never guesses: if detection fails, so does the request. Privacy is a kindness.

filters:blurclass(person)

Read the docs on redaction

Object removal

Mark a box and an inpainting model fills it in with what should be behind it. The reef keeps its coral, not the can.

filters:remove_region(40,120,300,200)

Read the docs on object removal

A studio in a shell.

Studio light for product shots, clean cut-outs, and sharper small pictures, like the blocky pearl in the shell. Each is one more step in the URL, run by a model you install on your server.

Studio mode

One filter cuts the product out and sets it on your brand color with a soft shadow, padded: its defaults. The color is set once on the server.

filters:studio(product)

−60 m · The Shipwreck

Signed, sealed, provable.

Some links should stay unreadable, some pictures should prove where they came from, and some addresses should never be fetched at all. Snap squeezes in through the hole in the hull.

  • Clickthe chest, or the wax seal on the desk · to seal your URL
  • Tapthe chest · to seal your URL

https://img.example.com/3843ad67…/crop:1200x630:smart/filters:sharpen(1.2):saturation(1.1)/root:photos/print.jpg

Clickthe chest to seal your URL · choice 5 of 5✓Sealed: the URL in the bar is one opaque token now · click again to open it

Sealed URLs

For links that stay public but unreadable: the whole recipe, operations and source, sealed into one opaque token in the signature slot. Only the server opens it, and it serves the same render.

s1.<token>/print.jpg

Read the docs on sealed URLs
Choice 5 of 5Seal it, or keep it readable

Here, with the chest, or with the wax seal on the captain’s desk.

Sealed hides the recipe. Readable shows it.

Readable is the right default for most links. Seal the ones that must be public and still keep their recipe to themselves.

Readable: the recipe stays in plain sight.

The ship’s log of your picture

  1. Ingredientroot:photos/print.jpg, the parent, named by its format
  2. Transformedcrop:1200x630:smart · sharpen(1.2):saturation(1.1)
  3. Signedas served, with your certificate

Provenance, checked and signed

Pictures can carry Content Credentials, a signed record of where they came from. crabcrop reports the record a source carries, and with your own certificate it signs every still JPEG, PNG, WebP, and AVIF it serves, with the source as its parent.

CRABCROP_C2PA_CERT · CRABCROP_C2PA_KEY

Read the docs on provenance
  1. photos.example.com/print.jpgfetched
  2. 10.0.0.7/admin.png403
  3. 169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data403
  4. 127.0.0.1:9000/backup.jpg403

Private sources blocked by default

The loader refuses sources on loopback, private, and other non-public addresses, checked again on every redirect. Allowlisting a host is how you vouch for an internal one.

403 source_forbidden CRABCROP_ALLOWED_SOURCES

Read the docs on private sources

−500 m · The Twilight Zone

It reads the picture.

Down here the light is yours: it follows your cursor.tap to shine it. What it finds, a meta answer names: tags with their scores, a line of alt text, the words in a bottle. And the URL can explain itself.

Here you can

  • Moveyour light over the creatures · to name them
  • Tapa creature to light it · and name it

This scene so far, as a meta answer would describe it. Light more creatures to add their tags.

{"width": 1200, "height": 630, "format": "jpeg","tags": [{ "label": "jellyfish", "score": 0.97 },{ "label": "message in a bottle", "score": 0.96 },{ "label": "anglerfish", "score": 0.93 },{ "label": "glowing worm", "score": 0.84 }],"alt_text": "Glowing jellyfish, a glowing worm, a message in a bottle and an anglerfish in the dark of the deep sea."}

Metadata that describes the picture

Ask for JSON instead of the picture and crabcrop describes it: size, format, provenance (meta mode, off by default: CRABCROP_META_MODE=1). Models you install add tags, alt text, and an aesthetic score; detections, moderation, embeddings, and OCR on request.

Accept: application/json; detections=1

Read the docs on metadata

The message in the bottle, read:

  1. To whoever finds this:0.98
  2. the print you’re after0.97
  3. sank past the warm vents.0.95
  4. Keep going! A friend0.91

Text recognition

Opt a meta request in and the answer reads the picture: the text lines in reading order, each with its box and a confidence score. The image bytes stay exactly the same.

Accept: application/json; ocr=1

Read the docs on text recognition

GET /explain/3843ad67…/crop:1200x630:smart/filters:sharpen(1.2):saturation(1.1)/root:photos/print.jpg

signature
valid · current key · never expires
source
root:photos/print.jpg · image · 2400 × 1600
crop
a 1200 × 630 window, moved to the subject
filters
sharpen 1.2, then saturation 1.1
format
none named: kept from the source, JPEG
forecast
1200 × 630 · JPEG

URLs that explain themselves

Put explain/ in front of the signature and the server answers with a report on the URL: the signature’s verdict, the source, every operation in plain words, and what will come out.

GET /explain/<signature>/…

Read the docs on explain

A tiny fish was lost in the dark. It followed your light all the way to Snap, and now he is taking it home.

−2,500 m · The Vents

The engine at the bottom.

Everything above runs on what is down here: one Rust binary, the libraries that build its URLs, and a server that agents can talk to. And in the glowing geode lies the source of it all.

$ curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -LsSf https://github.com/dayvson/crabcrop/releases/latest/download/crabcrop-installer.sh | sh

$ CRABCROP_SECRET=your-secret crabcrop

crabcrop listening on port 3000

One binary, built in Rust

Install it, give it a secret, and request images with the operations written into the URL. No pre-generated thumbnails, no build step: the URL is the API.

curl … crabcrop-installer.sh | sh

Read the docs on getting started 
import { buildURL } from "@crabcrop/url";const url = buildURL(base, secret,"crop:1200x630:smart/filters:sharpen(1.2):saturation(1.1)","root:photos/print.jpg");

→ https://img.example.com/3843ad67…/crop:1200x630:smart/filters:sharpen(1.2):saturation(1.1)/root:photos/print.jpg (the same from all three)

SDKs and loaders

Build and sign the same URL from TypeScript, Python, or the Rust crate the server verifies with. Loaders drop it into your framework’s image component:

  • Next.js
  • Nuxt
  • Hydrogen
  • Astro
  • SvelteKit

npm install @crabcrop/url

Read the docs on SDKs and loaders

The other little submarine down here is an agent. Its tool calls:

  1. agentsign_urlcrop:1200x630:smart/filters:sharpen(1.2):saturation(1.1) · root:photos/print.jpg
  2. crabcrophttps://img.example.com/3843ad67…/crop:1200x630:smart/filters:sharpen(1.2):saturation(1.1)/root:photos/print.jpg
  3. agentexplain_urlis it right?
  4. crabcropvalid · current key · 1200 × 630 · JPEG
  5. agentfetch_metawhat does it show?
  6. crabcrop1200 × 630 · JPEG · a crochet crab at a skate park, holding up a photo

MCP server for agents

Coding agents sign, explain, and inspect URLs through four tools over the same SDK: sign_url, explain_url, fetch_meta, and purge_result.

@crabcrop/mcp

Read the docs on the MCP server

Your URL comes along, so you can try other choices. Or keep scrolling: the sea starts over.

Signed in your browser with the sample secret demo-secret, on a stand-in host. Sign the same path with your own secret, on a server with a photos source root (and a background-removal model for a finish), and it serves the picture.
